title: How English merchants turned Douro wine into port
episode: Drunk Crusaders and Daring Traders: the Rise and Rise of Port
place: Port wine lodges, Cais de Gaia
description: Intoxicating History, a show about the history of drink, traces port from medieval trade to the English merchants who added brandy to Douro wine so it survived the voyage north. The wine still ages in lodges along this riverbank in Vila Nova de Gaia.

title: Port’s English story, told over the holidays
episode: 12 Days: Port wine and Darwin sets sail
place: Factory House, Rua do Infante Dom Henrique
description: Historians Tom Holland and Dominic Sandbrook spend part of this holiday episode on port and the British trade behind it. The Factory House, finished around 1790, was the private club of Porto’s British port shippers and still is.

title: The world’s oldest alliance, England and Portugal
episode: England & Portugal: The Oldest Alliance in the World
description: Historian Dan Snow on the alliance England and Portugal signed in 1386, which is still in force. The next year it was sealed in Porto Cathedral, where King João I married Philippa of Lancaster, an English princess.

episode: Portugal: The Golden Age of Discovery (Part 2)
description: Tom Holland and Dominic Sandbrook on how a small kingdom began sailing down the coast of Africa in the 1400s. Prince Henry, later called the Navigator, who backed the early voyages, is said to have been born in this house by the river in 1394.

title: Álvaro Siza, Porto’s great architect
description: An architecture show on Álvaro Siza, the Porto architect who won the Pritzker Prize in 1992. Siza studied at Porto’s architecture school and later designed its campus, a row of white buildings stepping down toward the Douro.
